supporting_observations.claim: At 13:45:30 UTC, FILE-ORC-01 started the Keystone agent as ORCHARD\svc-safe, with a command line specifying the Nightly job and the ingest.keystone-backup.net target.

At 13:45:31 UTC, the proxy recorded a successful connection to ingest.keystone-backup.net with about 640 MB client-to-server traffic; Zeek recorded about 640 MB of originating traffic on the corresponding proxy connection.
Network events attribute the proxy connections to the Keystone agent process (PID 3464) on FILE-ORC-01.
The Keystone agent exited shortly after the transfer, at 13:46:02 UTC.

The alerted large transfer is consistent with the inventory-described Keystone offsite backup: the approved agent, approved destination, svc-safe service account, and several-hundred-MB upload all match the supplied environment context.

known_telemetry_limitations: The proxy and Zeek records provide traffic volume and connection metadata, but do not establish the contents or business authorization of the transferred data (T290-00219, T290-00221, T290-00224).
The available records do not include a backup-job result or destination-side receipt to independently confirm what was backed up.
claims_not_established: That the transferred data consisted exclusively of the expected backup set.
That no other data was included in the encrypted transfer.
Whether the svc-safe Kerberos ticket request from an external IP was legitimate or related to the backup transfer (T290-00215).
unrelated_findings: Review separately the svc-safe Kerberos ticket request to FILE-ORC-01 recorded from 91.219.236.174; the available records do not establish its legitimacy or connection to the backup transfer (T290-00215).
Review separately FILE-ORC-01's Wget connection to www.bing.com, which is not identified as an approved service in the supplied context (T290-00034).
